newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end easier despite A share leap.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end easier despite A share leap.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market closed lower in thin trading on Tuesday despite solid gains in domestic A shares, with the B market's recent bearishness encouraging investors to cut their exposure and move to the sidelines, brokers said.
The B share index sank 1.33 points or 0.89 percent to 146.94, with turnover contracting to HK$51 million from HK$85 million on Monday.
In contrast, the A share index jumped 13.19 points or 2.93 percent to 463.59, partially helped by rises in market leader Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
Trading in the bank was suspended by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Monday afternoon due to volatile price movements and resumed Tuesday morning.

Turnover in the A share market shrank to 10.0 billion yuan from Monday's 14.5 billion yuan as some institutions held back, viewing the bank's suspension as a sign of tightened supervision by securities regulators, brokers said.
"The B share market's recent bearishness has prevented any fresh money inflow," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
"The big B share issue by Bengang Steel has also sucked out a lot of funds," the analyst said.
Bengang Steel Plates Co Ltd earlier this month completed an initial public offering of 460 million B shares, raising about one billion yuan.
The company has said it will list the B shares in Shenzhen in early July.
Brokers said they expected the B share trading over the next few days to be slow.
In the A share market, Shenzhen Development Bank ended the day up 1.67 yuan at 38.20 yuan on volume of 35 million shares, making it the most actively traded stock.

The bank's dividend proposal for 1996, consisting of a five-for-10 bonus issue and a cash dividend of 0.2 yuan per share, and investor optimism over the bank's earnings outlook, continued to generate buying interest, brokers said.
In a statement published in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times on Tuesday, the bank's board of directors said: "We think it is necessary to remind investors to be wary about surging prices".
Trading in the bank had been suspended for five sessions until last Friday for share trading irregularities. The bank closed up 10 percent last Friday and up 7.77 percent Monday morning session.
Northeast Pharmaceutical was among Tuesday's strongest A share performers, surging 0.81 yuan to 8.86 yuan.

In the B share market, television tube maker SEG Co maintained its sharp downward trend, falling HK$0.65 or 8.50 percent to HK$7.00 on volume of 609,803 shares. The issue lost 5.56 percent on Monday. Brokers provided no reason for the issue's decline.
Chenming Paper bucked the trend, firming HK$0.04 to HK$6.95 on volume of 1.8 million shares. It was the most actively traded B share.
